newsitem.title: FRANCE: French industrial production rebounds in February.
newsitem.headline: French industrial production rebounds in February.

text.p: French industrial production showed an unexpectedly strong rebound in February, official figures on Thursday showed, spurring hopes first-quarter gross domestic product could be more robust than forecast.

The signs of a healthier economy after months of gloomy news were also a boost for the ruling centre-right coalition, seeking re-election after a snap May/June parliamentary poll called by President Jacques Chirac earlier this week.

Industrial production, excluding construction, increased 1.6 percent in February after falling 1.1 percent in January, for a year-on-year rise of 1.6 percent, national statistics institute INSEE reported.

Industrial production stripping out energy, agri-food and construction -- seen by INSEE as the best guage of manufacturing output -- rose an even stronger 3.7 percent in February from the previous month, giving a year-on-year rise of 2.2 percent.
This measure of production fell 1.1 percent in January.

"It's a lot better than expected," said AMBN Amro economist Philippe Brossard. "They're very good numbers across the board. The year is starting out better than expected. It suggests the first quarter will be good".
He said he was looking for first-quarter growth of 0.6 percent. The government has forecast minimum growth in gross domestic product of 2.3 percent for full year 1997.
Brossard added that stronger growth would boost France's chances of meeting tough deficit targets to qualify for taking part in European monetary union.
Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais, said the numbers were positive and could help the centre-right's re-election hopes.

But another economist cautioned the strong performance needed to be treated with caution. "Industrial production figures can be very erratic. They will need to be confirmed," said Jean-Louis Mourier of Louis Dreyfus Finance.
Car sector output, struggling since the expiry of a state-sponsored rebate scheme last September, showed a strong turnaround, rising 5.1 percent in February after falling 0.6 percent in January.
"It says the car sector is doing much better than commentators have been saying," said Brossard.

Semi-finished goods production jumped 4.8 percent in February after falling 1.9 percent in January. And construction, which is not included in the headline figures, jumped 12.9 percent in February after falling 10.0 percent in January when cold weather conditions shut down many building sites.
